rejected.description: RBI’s New Window Could Beat US Treasury Yields But It Closes September 30 The RBI just made a decision that directly affects every NRI. If your dollar savings are sitting in a foreign bank account right now, the RBI just gave you a better option, one that could beat US treasury yields, and it closes September 30, 2026. It’s called an FCNR(B) deposit. You park your dollars directly in an Indian bank without converting to rupees. Your money stays in dollars, earns interest in dollars, and that interest is completely tax-free in India. Here’s what changed in June 2026. Normally, banks bear a hedging cost when raising foreign currency deposits, which limits the rates they can offer. The RBI is now bearing that cost on behalf of banks until September 30, 2026, and that saving gets passed directly to you as a depositor. Rates are already climbing well above previous levels, with some banks now offering 6-7% in USD. The last time RBI ran a similar scheme in 2013, it brought in tens of billions of dollars within months. Government backed. Dollar denominated. Tax-free in India.
